about:
Prince Manufacturing Corporation traces its roots to 1941, when John Prince opened a small machine shop on Water Street in Sioux City, Iowa, under the name Prince Hydraulics. His son Richard incorporated the business in September 1950 after securing a contract for 100 single-acting hydraulic cylinders, with Arthur C. Gall and F. John Roost joining as vice president and secretary/treasurer. The company now operates from North Sioux City, South Dakota.

Today Prince manufactures hydraulic cylinders and valves across multiple production facilities, all certified to ISO 9001:2015 by Amtivo. The product line includes welded-style cylinders and a range of hydraulic valves, supported by a product configurator, 3D CAD models, parts manuals, and how-to videos. The workforce numbers approximately 107 employees.

The company's early focus on the agricultural sector and the truck-and-trailer market remains central, though its hydraulic components now serve a broader industrial base. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket distributors seeking replacement cylinders and valves for mobile and stationary equipment.

Prince was founded to meet a specific demand for simple, reliable hydraulic cylinders, and the company emphasizes its quality management system as a differentiator, with every facility holding the same ISO 9001:2015 certification.
